transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
Federal agents search the Washington, D.C. home of Democratic Minnesota Congresswoman
Ilhan Omar Monday morning in an ongoing investigation linked to allegations of immigration fraud.
Her parents fled civil war in Somalia when she was a child, and they came to the U.S.
as refugees.
The impure as Barbara Spunt reports that Omar is a sharp critic and frequent target of President
Trump.
The Department of Justice says agents with Homeland Security investigations were executing
a judicially authorized search warrant, and that it's part of an ongoing federal criminal
investigation.
A spokesperson for the Congresswoman calls the search a "outrageous abuse of power and
an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political
enemies."
The search took place ahead of next month's midterm elections, in which Omar is seeking
reelection.
Vice President Vance has previously alleged Omar committed immigration fraud, something
she denies.
Barbara Spunt and PR News, Washington.
President Trump is back at the White House following a campaign rally in Ohio.
He ostensibly was there to boost Republican Senator John Husted's reelection campaign,
but he again attacked Congresswoman Omar and shouted out Congressman Max Miller, who was
facing domestic abuse allegations.
Trump also announced a new submarine component manufacturing center to be located in Cleveland.
U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia urging Americans to reconsider traveling to Saudi Arabia.
Multiple people have been killed in a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels
on Saudi airports in Birziah, Patraoui.
There have been at least four attacks on Riyadh's airport in the past week.
And this comes as the Houthis have been warning that Saudi airspace is a theater of war and
have been firing missiles and drones on Saudi airports and energy sites.
Now, Saudi authorities say 20 people were killed over the past week, but it was Saturday's
attack on Riyadh airport that was the deadliest.
Saudi authorities say 13 people of various nationalities were killed, including a U.S.
citizen, and that more than 300 others were wounded, some critically.
And then a day later, the airport was hit again.
New White House press secretary, Katie Zancariah, expected to hold her first briefing later
today, NPR's Brian Mann reports.
Katie Zancariah has worked and served on the advisory boards for conservative and anti-abortion
organizations.
She also appears often as a guest on right-leaning outlets, including Fox and News Nation.
After appointing her, Trump praised Zancariah's loyalty to himself, describing her as a devoted
fan.
Writing on social media, Zancariah said working for Trump would be the honor of a lifetime.
During an appearance in August on the network Real America's Voice, Zancariah described
abortion as the championing of death.
In social media posts in 2022, she amplified far-right conspiracy theories, including the
thoroughly debunked claim that former Democratic White House Chief of Staff John Podesta was
a pedophile.
Brian Mann, NPR News.
This is NPR.
Bulgaria's prime minister says he is seeking assistance from NATO and the European Union
after drones struck two ships in the Black Sea.
One of the ships sank and led to emergency rescue operations.
The prime minister said today that one crew member from his sunken vessel was rescued
but did not give details on the other's aboard.
Rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members from the other ship.
The prime minister says Bulgaria does not know who was responsible.
Nearly 14 million homes will hit the market over the next decade as boomers and other
older owners sell, but NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports that wave will not offer much help
to first-time buyers.
Coming years will see a 30 percent jump in housing inventory, according to a new analysis
by Realtor.com.
Most homes freed up will be larger, family-sized, and that could soften the market at a time
when many people are priced out.
But only a few hundred thousand will be smaller, so-called starter homes.
In part, the report says that's because those owners are more likely to have paid off their
mortgage and stay put longer.
This generational transfer will also play out slowly.
Housing analysts say the so-called silver tsunami is not likely to close the current
housing shortage.
The oldest baby boomers turn 80 this year, a turning point when homeownership starts
to decline.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
The best of seven National League Championship Series moving to Los Angeles, a game between
the Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers, is set for Wednesday.
The Brewers have a two-games-to-nothing lead following their victory, their seven-to-four
victory in Monday's game two.
This is NPR News.

Trump at White House after Ohio rally backing Senator John Husted, attacking Omar, announcing Cleveland submarine plant
